title: An empty 3D world does not explain itself.
intro: As the feature came together, internal feedback exposed a gap: an empty stage gave a new creator very little reason to begin. I designed two entry paths—continue an idea in the existing conversation, or explore an editable example first.
The examples showed different kinds of control: a riverside town, a casino infiltration and a desert race. Previewing a sample could communicate the result before the creator opened its scene.

items.title: Start with an idea
items.text: Connect a creative request to the scene it will produce.

items.title: Adjust the white blocks
items.text: Make scale and placement tangible through direct editing.

items.title: Shape the character’s path
items.text: Link the route in space to its timing.

items.title: Direct the camera
items.text: Connect camera movement with framing feedback.

items.title: Arrange the shots
items.text: Choose the views and rhythm of the sequence.

items.title: Return to the canvas
items.text: Export the rehearsal into the continuing creation workflow.

body: I organized guided practice around these six tasks in the native editor. It used a prepared replay rather than a live Agent run, without spending generation credits, and preserved the creator’s original project on exit.

I also worked on progressive scene feedback during generation, so creators could see work taking shape. The aim was to make waiting more understandable; this was not a claim that generation itself became faster.
